summary: A block of hairy skin from a University of Groningen (UMCG) dermatology module, showing its three layers: epidermis, dermis and subcutis. The front half is a solid cut block; the back half is opened up to show the hair follicles with their sebaceous glands and arrector pili, eccrine and apocrine sweat glands, the dermal blood vessel plexuses and the sensory nerves.
clinical: Superficial burns involve only the epidermis; partial-thickness burns reach the dermis but spare the deep hair follicles and sweat glands, whose epithelium regrows the surface. Full-thickness burns destroy these adnexa, so they cannot heal from within and usually need grafting.

Basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas arise from epidermal keratinocytes, melanoma from basal-layer melanocytes. For melanoma, the depth of invasion into the dermis (Breslow thickness) is the main predictor of spread and prognosis.

Big.name: Stratum corneum
Big.description: The outermost layer of the epidermis (golden): flattened dead keratinocytes (corneocytes) filled with keratin and bound by lipids. It forms the waterproof barrier and is continually shed and replaced from below, a cycle of about a month.

Epischdermis.name: Epidermis
Epischdermis.description: The living layers of the stratified squamous keratinising epidermis: keratinocytes of the stratum spinosum (joined by desmosomes) and stratum granulosum (keratohyalin granules) moving up from the basal layer. The epidermis has no blood vessels; its rete ridges interlock with the dermal papillae, which feed it by diffusion. It dips down into each hair follicle as the outer root sheath (the magenta sleeves around the follicles).

Extract6.name: Epidermis
Extract6.description: The living layers of the stratified squamous keratinising epidermis: keratinocytes of the stratum spinosum (joined by desmosomes) and stratum granulosum (keratohyalin granules) moving up from the basal layer. The epidermis has no blood vessels; its rete ridges interlock with the dermal papillae, which feed it by diffusion. It dips down into each hair follicle as the outer root sheath (the magenta sleeves around the follicles).

PM3D Cube3D2.name: Epidermis, back half (see-through)
PM3D Cube3D2.description: The full thickness of the epidermis over the opened back half, from stratum corneum down to the rete ridges, made translucent so the undulating dermo-epidermal junction and the dermal structures beneath can be seen.

PM3D Cube3D5 953.name: Stratum basale
PM3D Cube3D5 953.description: The single row of cuboidal basal cells (white beads) on the basement membrane at the dermo-epidermal junction. It is the dividing stem-cell layer that renews the epidermis, holds the melanocytes, and continues down each hair follicle as its outer root sheath.

PM3D Cube3D5 945.name: Dermis
PM3D Cube3D5 945.description: The connective tissue layer under the epidermis: a thin papillary layer of loose tissue in the dermal papillae and a thick reticular layer of dense irregular collagen and elastic fibres (pink), with scattered fibroblasts. It gives skin its strength and elasticity and carries the vessels, nerves and skin appendages.

PM3D Sphere3D2 343.name: Subcutaneous fat
PM3D Sphere3D2 343.description: The subcutis (hypodermis): lobules of adipocytes separated by fibrous septa, below the dermis. It insulates, cushions and stores energy, and carries the larger vessels and nerves that supply the skin.

Skin ZSphere 4.name: Hair
Skin ZSphere 4.description: Hair shafts of keratinised cells growing from the hair bulb at the base of each follicle. They emerge obliquely from the skin surface; melanin from bulb melanocytes gives the colour.

Extract1.name: Hair follicles and sebaceous glands
Extract1.description: Hair follicles (orange) are tubes of epidermis sunk deep into the dermis, ending in the hair bulb around a dermal papilla. The lobulated sebaceous gland beside each follicle empties oily sebum into it by holocrine secretion; blocked, inflamed pilosebaceous units cause acne.

PM3D Sphere3D2 2.name: Arrector pili muscle
PM3D Sphere3D2 2.description: A small band of smooth muscle running obliquely from the hair follicle to the papillary dermis. Sympathetic stimulation (cold, fear) contracts it, standing the hair up and dimpling the skin into 'goose bumps'.

Skin ZSphere29 11.name: Eccrine sweat glands
Skin ZSphere29 11.description: Coiled tubular glands in the deep dermis whose ducts run straight up and spiral through the epidermis to open on the skin surface. Found almost everywhere, they secrete watery sweat for heat loss and are supplied by sympathetic cholinergic fibres.

Extract8.name: Eccrine sweat glands
Extract8.description: Coiled tubular glands in the deep dermis whose ducts run straight up and spiral through the epidermis to open on the skin surface. Found almost everywhere, they secrete watery sweat for heat loss and are supplied by sympathetic cholinergic fibres.

Extract3 1.name: Apocrine sweat gland
Extract3 1.description: A coiled sweat gland whose duct opens into the upper hair follicle rather than onto the skin surface. Apocrine glands are found mainly in the axilla and anogenital region, become active at puberty, and their protein-rich secretion is broken down by skin bacteria to produce body odour.

Skin ZSphere6.name: Blood vessels
Skin ZSphere6.description: Arteries (red) and veins (blue) forming two plexuses parallel to the surface: a deep one at the dermis-subcutis border and a superficial (subpapillary) one, linked by vertical vessels and sending capillary loops into the dermal papillae. Dermal blood flow is adjusted to regulate body temperature.

Skin ZSphere7.name: Nerves
Skin ZSphere7.description: Sensory nerve fibres (pale yellow) branching through the dermis; the finest end as free nerve endings among the epidermal cells, sensing pain, temperature and itch.

notes: Hidden: the part named 'Epidermis' is not tissue but the black side label card with bracket lines and the words Epidermis / Dermis / Subcutis. Apocrine gland identity (Extract3 1) is inferred from its duct running up to end in the upper hair follicle, unlike the eccrine ducts that reach the surface; not labelled by the creator. 'Extract6' (magenta sheet with rete ridges that continues down the follicles and around the sebaceous gland) and 'Epischdermis' (front-half cell layers) are both treated as the living epidermis layers; the translucent 'PM3D Cube3D2' block over the back half is presumably the whole epidermis made see-through. Hair follicles and sebaceous glands are one mesh and cannot be separated. The vessels are one mesh with red/blue vertex colours (arteries and veins not separable). Subcutaneous fat recoloured from lemon yellow to the golden tone of the creator's thumbnail. No atlas links: all parts are microscopic. Verifier: 'PM3D Cube3D2' spans the full epidermal height (same top as the stratum corneum, same rete-ridge base as the living layers), so it is named as the whole back-half epidermis rather than just its surface.
